name: MonarchVideoThumbnail
title: VideoThumbnail
summary: A poster for a video with a round play mark and a badge that shows its length. With onPlay the whole thumbnail is one button.
whenToUse: In a list or a grid of videos, an attachment, or a message, where tapping the poster starts the video.
whenNotToUse: To play the video in place use the app's player (Media3) in a MonarchFilePreview player slot. For a still image use Image.
api: @Composable fun MonarchVideoThumbnail(title: String, image: Painter?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onPlay: (() -> Unit)? = null, durationMillis: Long? = null, aspectRatio: Float? = null, contentScale: ContentScale = ContentScale.Crop, showPlayIcon: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, playLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
suspend fun captureVideoFrame(context: Context, uri: Uri, timeMillis: Long? = null): ImageBitmap?

options.name: title
options.description: What the video shows, already localised. Read by TalkBack; not drawn. Empty gives the built-in "Video".

options.name: image
options.description: The poster the app loaded, or null while there is none.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the thumbnail. It fills the width it is given.

options.name: onPlay
options.description: Makes the thumbnail a button that calls this.

options.name: durationMillis
options.description: The length, shown as 1:05 or 1:01:05 and spoken in words.

options.name: aspectRatio
options.description: Width divided by height. 16 to 9 when null or not positive.

options.name: contentScale
options.description: Crop fills the frame; Fit letterboxes the poster on the inverse fill.

options.name: showPlayIcon
options.description: Draws the round play mark over the poster.

options.name: playLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the button, "Play <title>".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions of the button.

states.name: poster
states.description: The image crops or fits the frame, with the play mark in the middle.

states.name: placeholder
states.description: While image is null: the inverse fill with a muted play glyph and no round mark.

states.name: button
states.description: With onPlay: one button with a focus ring and the ripple.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The play disc uses the muted background and the triangle the disabled text color; taps do nothing.

appearance: The frame has 12dp corners on the inverse background. The play mark is a 48dp disc in the surface color with the medium shadow and a triangle in the default text color; the badge is the inverse background with inverse text in the caption style with tabular figures. Each role has its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web captures a frame from the video in the browser when no thumbnail is given. Here, as on iOS, the view takes a poster by the image convention (a Painter) and frame capture is the separate suspend function captureVideoFrame, built on the platform MediaMetadataRetriever, whose result the app passes as a BitmapPainter; the web's onCaptureError is the exception it throws. The web's translucent play disc and badge are opaque here, because Monarch takes colors by role and does not dim. The length is in milliseconds (durationMillis), as in the Android media APIs, where the web and iOS take seconds. The web's loading pulse is not drawn, because the thumbnail never captures on its own.
accessibility: With onPlay it is one element with the button role named "Play <title>", or playLabel.
Without onPlay it is one element with the image role named by the title.
The length is its state description, in words for the current locale ("1 minute, 5 seconds"); the badge digits are not read.
The thumbnail is as wide as its container, far above 48dp, and draws the Monarch focus ring.
The badge text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: A negative length is shown as 0:00; lengths are rounded to whole seconds.
A title of spaces gives the built-in "Video".
captureVideoFrame keeps the time inside the video and returns null when there is no frame there; a URI it cannot open throws.
With showPlayIcon false the poster has no mark, but the button still works.

examples.title: With a poster and duration
examples.code:
MonarchVideoThumbnail(
    title = "Product overview",
    image = sampleThumbnailPainter(),
    durationMillis = 65 * 1_000L,
)

examples.title: A poster captured from the video

parityExceptions.reason: The duration is drawn on the thumbnail as 1:05 but hidden from the semantics tree, which carries the spoken form "1 minute, 5 seconds" instead.
parityExceptions.convention: TalkBack reads a duration in words, not as a clock
